messages:
kevin (customer): hey folks, after we moved the Dedicated cluster behind our VPC LB + istio sidecars some production requests are intermittently returning 401 from the model gateway. only affects requests routed through the L7 chain, direct calls to the gateway from an internal host are fine. repro steps and logs below. please help, customer is seeing burst of auth failures during spikes.

anya (support): thanks, can you paste a minimal repro and the exact headers the gateway receives? 401 usually means the Authorization header got stripped or the token audience changed.

kevin (customer): repro: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \"https://dedicated.example.internal/v1/engines/redwood/complete\"
Output (from LB->gateway access log):
  "GET /v1/engines/redwood/complete" 401 - - "-" 0.002
Gateway auth log: "missing authorization header"
When I tcpdump on node before istio: I see Authorization present. After envoy sidecar egress: header absent.

rob (infra): hmm, that points at an Envoy filter or Istio ext_authz removing or normalizing headers. are you using an external ext-auth service (oauth proxy) in front of the gateway?

kevin (customer): yes we have an ext-authz configured in Istio for SSO enforcement at the mesh edge. it's an external auth server that returns 200 + headers. we also have an nginx LB that terminates TLS and forwards to the istio ingress.

anya (support): common traps: (1) Envoy's ext_authz can be configured in HTTP mode to "shadow" or "check" but may also strip headers unless "include_request_headers_in_check" or "response_headers_to_add" are configured. (2) Some ingress proxies purposely remove Authorization for security unless passthrough configured. can you share snippets of your Istio AuthorizationPolicy / extAuthz config?

kevin (customer): here's the relevant snippet from istio ext-auth policy: 
```
apiVersion: "security.istio.io/v1beta1"
kind: "RequestAuthentication"
metadata:
  name: sso-jwt
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway-proxy
  jwtRules:
  - issuer: "https://idp.example/"
    jwksUri: "https://idp.example/.well-known/jwks.json"
```
And we have an EnvoyFilter that calls the ext-authz svc. I can paste if helpful.

julian (platform): another place to check: nginx config. if it does `proxy_set_header Authorization "";` or uses `proxy_hide_header` that would drop it. also some cloud LB managed services rewrite headers to `x-forwarded-authorization`. do you see any `x-forwarded-authorization` on the gateway logs?

kevin (customer): good call — gateway logs sometimes show `X-Forwarded-Authorization: <redacted>`, but Authorization absent. when we changed nginx to `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Authorization $http_authorization;` and removed `proxy_set_header Authorization`, the gateway got nothing in Authorization.

rob (infra): that's expected: many app stacks only inspect Authorization header. two remediation paths: (A) configure the edge to preserve Authorization and forward it verbatim, or (B) update the gateway/sidecar to accept X-Forwarded-Authorization as a fallback. option A is preferable for token binding.

anya (support): quick diagnostic commands:
```
# check envoy filters that manipulate headers
kubectl -n istio-system get envoyfilter -o yaml | grep -i authorization -C3
# dump ingress pod env
kubectl -n prod exec -it <ingress-pod> -- env | grep -i nginx
# tcpdump inside sidecar to confirm drop point
kubectl -n prod exec -it <pod> -- tcpdump -A -s 0 -nn -c 50 'port 443'
```

kevin (customer): I ran the grep on envoyfilters and found this block in our custom filter: 
```
- applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
  match:
    context: GATEWAY
  patch:
    operation: INSERT_AFTER
    value:
      name: envoy.filters.http.lua
      typed_config:
        "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
        inlineCode: |
          function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
            -- strip internal cookies
            request_handle:headers():remove("authorization")
          end
```
We added that LUA to remove internal Authorization when calls originate from our control plane. maybe it's overbroad.

anya (support): aha, that explains it. the Lua filter is the culprit. it unconditionally removes Authorization at the gateway context. do you have route metadata to only apply it for control-plane clients? if not, change the Lua to: 
```
if request_handle:headers():get("x-internal-origin") == "control-plane" then
  request_handle:headers():remove("authorization")
end
```
That will preserve customer Authorization tokens.

kevin (customer): ok will try. quick question: why does direct internal traffic bypass this?

rob (infra): because the EnvoyFilter match is scoped to the GATEWAY context and your internal test requests probably hit the service directly without passing through that global gateway filter. When you go through nginx -> ingressgateway the filter is executed.

kevin (customer): deployed the guarded lua change, restarted ingress pods. initial tests look good — Authorization now passes and gateway accepts the Bearer token. will run load test to confirm spike behavior.

anya (support): great. please leave this thread open until you've validated under load. if spike still causes intermittent 401s after fix, we'll look at token expiry, jwks caching (504s on idp), and ext-authz timeouts.

ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-3125 (assigned to rob).

rob (infra): I'll follow up to add a regression test to prevent future accidental header-strip patches. also will add a lint step: warn if any EnvoyFilter contains `remove("authorization")` without route-based guards.

kevin (customer): thanks everyone, initial load run looks stable. will keep monitoring for 30m then mark resolved. :white_check_mark:
